messages:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH — Customer Cobalt (Cobalt-Prod VPC, us-west-2) experiencing elevated 5xx and NLB target instability on private inference endpoints. Alert: nlb_unhealthy_target_ratio > 50%. Paging oncall. https://redwood.incidents/c/5248501234

oncall-jess: Oncall Jess here, acknowledging. Assigning net-harper + eng-ops-ryan to investigate. Will keep customer looped via CS.

net-harper: Checking NLB target health and recent SG changes. Running: ```aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:111:targetgroup/tg-cobalt --region us-west-2```

eng-ops-ryan: Also running tcpdump on a model node to see egress resets: ```sudo tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp port 443 and tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-rst|tcp-fin) != 0' -c 200 -w /tmp/cobalt.pcap```

net-harper: Results: 12/20 targets UNHEALTHY. Reasons: "502" + "health check failed". I can see recent security group rules updated in config history (ephemeral port block).

cs-lina: @cs-lina (CS): Cobalt SRE confirmed they pushed a tightened egress firewall ~2m before alerts. They're reverting the change now, but want us to run mitigation while they revert.

oncall-jess: Plan: 1) Fail traffic to backup NLB (Route53 weighted shift) to reduce customer impact, 2) Temp open SG egress (1024-65535 -> 443) for our model subnets, 3) Re-evaluate target health, 4) Coordinate with customer for permanent fix.

eng-ops-ryan: Executing Route53 change to shift 100% traffic to backup NLB. Command used: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3EXAMPLE --change-batch file://shift-to-backup.json``` (shift-to-backup.json contains weighted records pointing to backup NLB).

net-harper: Applied temporary SG rule allowing outbound 1024-65535 -> 443 from model subnets. Healthchecks recovering: 8/20 -> 15/20 within 90s.

incident-bot: Timeline note: 5248501234 - initial pager; 5248501350 - Route53 weight shift applied; 5248501420 - SG temp rule applied; 5248501480 - target health recovery trend observed.

oncall-jess: Monitoring metrics — 5xx rate fell from ~48% to ~2% over 5 minutes. Latency stable. Eng-ops: confirm backend pool warm and steady.

cs-lina: Cobalt confirms they reverted their egress rule. They will submit an audited rollback and want a postmortem.

eng-ops-ryan: Starting controlled rollback of Route53: set canary 10% to primary for 5m, then shift 100% if stable. Command: ```aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://canary.json```

net-harper: Removed temp SG rule after verifying health & metrics stable. Done.

oncall-jess: Status: RESOLVED (for now). Root cause: customer-side egress firewall change blocking ephemeral ports used by NLB health checks/backchannel. Impact: short period of increased 5xx for Cobalt traffic. Remediation: temporary failover + SG adjustment while customer reverted config. Follow-up: playbook update to auto-detect outbound egress changes and an automated failover checklist.

cs-lina: I'll open customer-facing incident report and schedule joint postmortem for tomorrow 10:00 PST.

oncall-jess: Handing off to @oncall-next. Handoff notes: monitor Cobalt endpoints for 30m, watch NLB unhealthy target ratio and error rate, verify scheduled customer changes don't reappear. :white_check_mark:
